story: Stage 11 delivered plenty of racing drama, even if the day ended without an official stage winner. From early on,Eventually, a trio made it clear. They gained time but were reeled in with around 70 kilometers to go. But just as the race heated up, race organizers made an unusual call: due to safety concerns, no stage winner would be awarded, and general classification times would be taken at the 3 km to go mark. That didn’t stop the GC contenders from testing each other on the brutally steep Alto del Pike. João Almeida was the first to attack, but he was quickly countered by Jonas Vingegaard, who looked strong on the climb. Tom Pidcock bridged across and tried to distance Vingegaard in the final meters of the ascent. Pidcock gained a small gap over the top — but Vingegaard clawed him back on the descent, keeping the GC standings tight heading into Stage 12.
